answer: Agents bid on a voyage delivering nectar drinks to a lagoon resort. Each bid includes a nonce whose hash with the bid, sender key and a short-lived market challenge is below a fixed target. The gateway checks it cheaply and accepts each proof once, with no free quota for new accounts. A million aliases cannot reuse one proof or reset the work required per bid. Assuming costly hashing without shortcuts, each accepted bid needs fresh expected work. This limits cheap flooding, not wealthy attackers or coordinated lying.
